en: An ace pitcher for the Tokyo Gigants, with 197 wins to his name. He faced off with the rookie Shinada fifteen years ago, who he also pitched to in his high school years. He was involved in the gambling scandal on the Gigants side. He had an agreement to take over the Nagoya Family from Fujita after fifteen years, and joined the Wyverns in a trade. He wanted a rematch after Shinada hit his seventh pitch into the stands all those years ago, but Shinada anticipated his curveball, and prevailed again.

He batted fourth for the Wyverns when the gambling scandal took place fifteen years ago. After retiring, he opened a successful yakiniku restaurant in town. Though he knew of the backroom dealings at the time, he did what he was told to prolong his career. He warns Shinada that digging too deep into the past could cost him his life.

He batted fourth for the Wyverns when the gambling scandal took place fifteen years ago. After retiring, he opened a successful yakiniku restaurant in town. Though he knew of the backroom dealings at the time, he did what he was told to prolong his career. He warned Shinada that digging too deep into the past could cost him his life. He fought Shinada after Ushijima failed to silence him, but chose defeat so that Shinada could learn the truth. Though he turned himself in at Ushijima's behest, he was soon released.

He was the Wyverns' second baseman during the baseball scandal fifteen years ago, but had been benched to make way for Shinada. After retiring, he did construction work in Kineicho. He went to great lengths to protect the Nagoya Family, even killing a man cornered by Shinada by dropping scaffolding on him. Ironically, he was also killed to prevent him from spilling secrets.

The former fourth chairman of the Tojo Clan. A legendary yakuza once called the Dragon of Dojima. After making a clean break, he ran Morning Glory Orphanage in Okinawa with Haruka, daughter of his childhood love Yumi. While working as a taxi driver in Nagasugai, Fukuoka under the alias Taichi Suzuki, he became embroiled in the events surrounding Daigo's disappearance. Asked by Madarame to protect Fukuoka's future, he took on the Tojo Clan for the Yamagasa Family and won. He has returned to Kamurocho after Morinaga told him he'd find answers there.

A legendary yakuza who spent 25 years behind bars, accused of killing eighteen members of a rival organization. Two years ago he rejoined the Tojo Clan as a patriarch. He agreed to serve as Tojo Clan captain, but chose to go to prison to pay for his crimes first. However, hearing of Majima's death, he broke out and went to Tsukimino for answers. After Baba's betrayal, he learned there was a mastermind behind the plot and struck a deal with an Osaka detective to go to Tokyo. Upon arriving in Kamurocho, he is told to seek out Morinaga.

A girl who was caught up in the ten billion yen incident. She was living with Kiryu at the orphanage in Okinawa, but was scouted by Park and moved to Osaka to enter show business. When Park suddenly dies, she and Akiyama discover Ousaka Enterprises had a hand in her death. Learning that Park's ex-husband Majima planned to meet her in Tokyo, Haruka heads there to perform her debut concert and fulfill her promise to Park. She is now training at a studio in Kamurocho.

The owner of moneylender Sky Finance in Kamurocho. He had been frequenting Osaka to open a branch in Sotenbori, but after Park's death he was reunited with Haruka at Dyna Chair. Through their investigation, they discovered Ousaka Enterprises' involvement. With Haruka's life in danger, he took her to Tokyo to ensure Park's dream was fulfilled. In Kamurocho, Katsuya asked him to cancel the concert for 500 million yen, but he refuses to give up on Haruka and Park's dream.

A batter for the Nagoya Wyverns fifteen years ago. After hitting a home run in his first game, he was permanently banned on suspicion of involvement in a baseball gambling scandal. Since then he's lived as a nightlife journalist in Kineicho. He started looking into a gambling incident for Dojima, who wanted to unmask the Nagoya Family. After Sawada told him that the Kuroha Family of the Omi Alliance was involved, and they had something planned for Haruka's concert, he goes to Sky Finance to get the money needed to stop it.

Bodyguard to Tojo Clan Chairman Daigo Dojima. He is normally silent at Morinaga's side, but once riled up it's hard to calm him down. He was put in a tight spot after Daigo disappeared following the talks with Madarame in Nagasugai, and searched for him frantically with Morinaga. He was thought to be killed by Morinaga, though he survived. However, he felt abandoned by Morinaga after he betrayed Aoyama, and went to Tokyo to ask his intentions. Saejima found him with the Florist of Sai, trying to learn Morinaga's whereabouts. They fought in the Underground Coliseum.

Current chairman of the Tojo Clan, which at 30,000 members is the largest yakuza group in Kanto. He suspected something was amiss when he learned that Omi Alliance Seventh Chairman Kurosawa was ill. Together with Majima, he planned to use this chance to clear out any traitors. He confronted Kurosawa on the rooftop of Kamurocho Hills, but was shot from behind by Kanai.

A militant yakuza, once feared as the Mad Dog of Shimano. He and Saejima are sworn brothers who pledged to hold the Tojo Clan together. After Dojima caught on to Kurosawa's plans, Majima helped him smoke out traitors by allying with regional yakuza groups. He used to be married to Mirei Park and helped Katsuya set up Osaka Talent, but he left after feeling he was getting in the way of Park's dreams.

Runs Osaka Talent, the leading talent agency in Kansai. He is also a yakuza who holds the posts of Omi Alliance chief of headquarters and chairman of Ousaka Enterprises. He admonished Kanai for going after Majima ahead of the impending East-West war, but went to Tokyo to position himself as successor to the seventh Omi chairman.

Known as the most militant in the Omi Alliance now that Ryuji Goda, the Dragon of Kansai, is gone. He laments the weakened state of the Tojo Clan, and visits Kiryu in Fukuoka to persuade him to rejoin so he can have a worthy opponent. He took a neutral stance in the battle between the Tojo Clan and the Yamagasa Family, and witnessed Kiryu's power for himself. After returning to Kansai to prepare for the coming war, he heard Katsuya had made a move, so he headed to Tokyo with his soldiers.

Captain of Ousaka Enterprises, which controls Sotenbori. He is as tough as his massive frame suggests, to the point where little fazes him. After growing frustrated at Katsuya's indecisiveness as others vie for the Omi throne, he decided to go after Majima alone. His actions led to the death of Park and put Horie in the hospital, but he failed to produce results and incurred Katsuya's wrath. In the end, he betrayed Katsuya and sided with Kurosawa. He showed up at Kamurocho Hills and took down Daigo.

Current chairman of the Omi Alliance, Kansai's largest yakuza group. To crush the Tojo Clan as well as the Omi Alliance, he told Daigo he was terminally ill so he would send his top men out where they were vulnerable to assassination. He then pretended to be a detective and brought potential rivals, like Kiryu, together so they would fight. After the showdown at Kamurocho Hills, he ambushed and shot his weakened foes, telling them that Haruka was in danger.

A detective with the organized crime unit of the Osaka Prefectural Police. He is trying to stop the impending war between the Omi Alliance and the Tojo Clan without involving the Tokyo Metropolitan Police. He asks Kiryu and others to help calm the coming storm while avoiding direct involvement himself. After bringing Saejima to Kamurocho from Sapporo, he asks him to find Morinaga.

A detective who has built up a rapport with Kiryu and the others, after working together in the ten billion yen incident. He handed in his badge for a time and worked as a newspaper reporter focusing on politics, but rejoined the force two years ago. He continues to have a good relationship with the mama of New Serena. While investigating the murder of Fujita at a Tokyo hotel, he found indications that Katsuya was involved.

Owner of the New Serena lounge in Kamurocho. Date helped her out when she started her business, so she always gives special treatment to Kiryu and the others. She was once married to a policeman, but he was killed in the line of duty. She fears the same could happen to Date, and so has avoided getting involved with him as more than a customer, but in the last few years they've grown close. With Kiryu's return to Kamurocho, she has offered to let him use New Serena as a base.

The boss of an underground organization in Purgatory and a legendary information dealer with many sources. He earned his name from the bouquets he hands out, with information recorded on the attached card. He has provided tips to Kiryu and Saejima in the past, but always gives them a special task to complete in lieu of payment.

Haruka's vocal coach. She was once a singer herself, but now works behind the scenes. After Park's sudden death, she and Horie do their best to help Haruka make her debut, and when Horie is hospitalized she takes over as Haruka's manager. When it is revealed that Park had planned a concert at Japan Dome for Haruka's debut, though intimidated, she does her best to organize the event. Once Nakai reveals the plans for a special unit with T-Set, she focuses on vocal training for the trio.

A famous dance instructor. He rarely takes the stage himself, but is known throughout the world for his ability to extract talent from those he teaches. He doesn't seek money or power, and only instructs those he sees potential in. He met Haruka while in Japan to prepare for a concert and agreed to train her. After Park's death, when Haruka's debut is threatened by the interference of Ousaka Enterprises, he supports Yamaura in preparing for the concert. He is now giving special training to Haruka at a studio in Kamurocho in the short time before her concert.

T-Set's manager. He didn't let up even after Park's death, goading Haruka into promising to join Osaka Talent if she loses to T-Set in the Princess League Finals, but also recognizes her ability. He showed up as Haruka was preparing for her debut concert in Tokyo and told her about Dream Line, the special unit Park had planned with Katsuya before her death.

A member of the T-Set idol group. Park was the one who discovered her and she signed with Dyna Chair first, but later moved to Osaka Talent after they had a falling out. She believes in earning your place and looked down on Haruka because of her inexperience, leading to conflict between them at times. However, she saw Haruka's talent through her Princess League performances and recognized her as a rival. She acts disappointed about forming Dream Line with Haruka, but inside she's actually excited.

A member of the T-Set idol group. Park was the one who discovered her and she signed with Dyna Chair first, but later moved to Osaka Talent with Mai after they had a falling out. Like Mai, she didn't take to Haruka at first, but over the course of the Princess League she is forced to admit that Haruka is a strong competitor. Since the news about forming Dream Line, she has been working on polishing her performance to an ever higher level.

Saejima's cellmate in prison. He treated Saejima like an older brother, but all the stories about his past had been lies. He was really sent to Abashiri to monitor Saejima and make sure he came to Tsukimino at the right time, using Kugihara to control the timing of his release. After losing a fight with Saejima, he headed to Tokyo. There he found Kiryu, and gave him details that would help him discover the truth.
